Round-Ups Plaid

Connect a debit or credit card. Every time you spend, we round the purchase up to the nearest dollar and set the spare change aside for your fund — swept over automatically once a week.

How it works

Grocery Store$62.10  → +$0.90
Gas Station$38.50  → +$0.50

Estate Planning Checklist

The industry-standard checklist, with the charitable decision flagged at every point it belongs. Progress saves in this browser only — nothing is transmitted.

Nine areas, fifty-three items. Mark anything that doesn’t apply and it drops out of the count.

Bring this to the people who can act on it

An estate attorney drafts and executes the documents. The tax advisor prices the moves. A Cleveland Foundation gift planner can confirm how a gift is accepted and how a fund is structured.

This checklist is general educational information, not legal, tax, or financial advice, and it does not create an advisory relationship. Rules on taxes, trusts, and charitable deductions change and vary by state and by situation. Confirm exemption amounts, contribution limits, and distribution rules that apply in the current year with the client’s own attorney and tax advisor before acting.

Legacy & Estate Giving

Leave Your Legacy

There are several ways to leave a lasting philanthropic legacy at the Cleveland Foundation. Explore the options below — or talk to Jordan Reyes to find the right fit.

Charitable Bequest
Leave a gift in your will. Learn how bequests work and what language to use.
Retirement Account Designation
Name TCF as beneficiary of an IRA or 401(k). Often more tax-efficient than a bequest.
Life Insurance Gift
Name TCF as owner or beneficiary of a life insurance policy.
Talk to Jordan
Free, confidential conversation about what legacy giving could look like for you.
